name: Negotiation
description: Tactical empathy, anchoring, concession management, BATNA preservation, and emotional control.

dimensions.name: Anchoring & Framing
dimensions.description: Setting psychological anchor, framing terms around mutual value, controlling baseline.

rubricCriteria.90-100: Anchors strategically with objective justification; controls terms of debate.
rubricCriteria.70-89: Reasonable anchor, slight hesitation when counter-anchored.
rubricCriteria.50-69: Accepts counterparty's hostile anchor without pushback.
rubricCriteria.0-49: Bids against self; makes concessions before counterparty even asks.

dimensions.name: Concession Trading (If-Then)
dimensions.description: Never giving anything away for free; demanding reciprocal value for every shift.

rubricCriteria.90-100: Strict 'If we do X, you must do Y' trade-offs; protects key commercial terms.
rubricCriteria.70-89: Trades concessions well but gives away minor points without equivalent return.
rubricCriteria.50-69: Gives away price or scope unilaterally to be 'polite'.

dimensions.name: Tactical Empathy & Calibrated Questions
dimensions.description: Using 'How' and 'What' calibrated questions; labeling counterpart's unspoken fears.

rubricCriteria.90-100: Masterful mirroring and labeling; turns adversary into joint problem-solver.
rubricCriteria.70-89: Good listening; asks productive questions with minor defensiveness.
rubricCriteria.50-69: Interrupts counterparty; focuses only on own demands.
